title: The Holocaust: the mechanics of a genocide
subject: histoire
description: Between **1941** and **1945**, the Nazi regime organized the murder of six million Jews. The Holocaust was not a sudden burst of hatred. It was a process run by a state.

hero.hook: How a modern state turned persecution into extermination.

blocks.text: Between **1941** and **1945**, the Nazi regime organized the murder of **6 million Jews**, two thirds of the Jews of Europe. In Hebrew, **Shoah** means “catastrophe.”
This genocide was not disorderly violence. It was a state process, built step by step, from legal exclusion to industrial killing.

From **January 1933**, when **Adolf Hitler** came to power, the Nazi state wrote antisemitism into law. The Nuremberg Laws (**1935**) stripped Jews of their citizenship and banned mixed marriages. In November **1938**, Kristallnacht, an organized **[[pogrom]]** (a violent attack on a Jewish community), left synagogues burned and **30,000** men interned.

After the invasion of Poland (**1939**), the Nazis imposed **[[ghettoization]]**: Jews were shut into sealed districts, notably in Warsaw and Lodz. Hunger, disease, isolation. The destruction was already massive, though still indirect.

blocks.caption: Auschwitz-Birkenau, which became the symbol of the extermination system

sections.title: The invasion of the USSR and the shootings

blocks.text: On **June 22, 1941**, Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa against the USSR. Behind the Wehrmacht, the German army, came the **[[Einsatzgruppen]]**, mobile SS units that shot communists and Jewish civilians.

In roughly **18 months**, these squads killed close to **1.5 million** people. At Babi Yar, near Kyiv, in September **1941**, **33,771** Jews were shot in two days. The method was judged too slow, too visible, too hard on the men who carried it out. The regime went looking for something more anonymous.

sections.title: Wannsee: organizing murder across a continent

blocks.text: On **January 20, 1942**, [[The Wannsee Conference]] brought **15** senior Nazi officials together near Berlin. The principle of extermination had already been settled. What they organized was the deportation of every Jew in Europe: trains, paperwork, logistics.

blocks.caption: The Wannsee villa, where the “Final Solution” was coordinated

blocks.text: Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka and Auschwitz-Birkenau became killing centers. On the ramp, a “selection” separated a minority sent to forced labor from the majority taken straight to the gas chambers. The philosopher **Hannah Arendt** would later describe this as [[The "banality of evil"]]: extermination handled like an administrative problem.
The Wannsee Conference, which coordinated a crime on a continental scale, lasted about **90 minutes**.

sections.title: The toll and the duty of memory

blocks.text: Of the **9 million** Jews living in Europe before the war, two thirds were killed. Poland lost about **90%** of its Jewish population. The regime also persecuted **[[Gypsies]]** (Roma and Sinti), disabled people, homosexuals and political opponents. The Holocaust remains unique in its aim: the total, systematic destruction of a people.

The Nuremberg trials then tried to give the crime a legal name. Places such as **[[Yad Vashem]]**, the memorial institute in Jerusalem, keep the memory alive so that this state machinery is neither forgotten nor treated as ordinary.

blocks.text: The Holocaust was the murder of **6 million** Jews by a state system: legal exclusion, ghettos, mass shootings, then killing centers. An organized genocide, not a spontaneous explosion.
